stories.head: Iran fires drones at US radar in Bahrain for third time in days
stories.say: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they launched drones at a US radar system in Bahrain on Tuesday, their third attack on US targets there in days. Bahrain says its defences intercepted them.
stories.stand: Bahrain says its air defences stopped the attack, as a third US aircraft carrier group arrives in the region.
body: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they launched a drone attack on a US radar system at Isa airbase in Bahrain on Tuesday. Bahrain said its air defences intercepted the drones, and there appeared to be little or no damage.

It was the third Iranian attack on US military targets in Bahrain since Friday, after a roughly two-month lull in Iranian strikes on Arab neighbours. Residents of Manama received a mobile alert and blasts were heard over the capital before an all clear.

US Central Command confirmed the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group had arrived, joining the USS George H.W. Bush and USS George Washington. Iran said the attacks answered US violations of its airspace. Qatar-led mediation has stalled.

stories.head: Ukraine strikes Kerch Bridge to Crimea for second day, road arch collapses
stories.say: Ukraine has hit the bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea for a second day, and says a road arch collapsed. Russia says it downed more than fourteen hundred drones overnight.
stories.stand: Two people were killed in Crimea, Russian-installed officials said, as Russia reported its largest overnight drone attack of the war.
body: Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge, the 19km road and rail link between southern Russia and occupied Crimea, for a second day on Tuesday. Crimea's Russian-installed governor, Sergei Aksyonov, said two people were killed and traffic was suspended.

Ukraine's General Staff said a road arch and span collapsed, while the rail section still stands. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the operation unprecedented and said it was retaliation for Russian strikes on infrastructure.

Russia's defence ministry said it shot down 1,441 drones over 22 regions, a record. Kyiv's mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said Russian strikes hit the city's North and South bridges and partly cut power and water.

stories.head: Ukraine holds peace talks with US and European officials
stories.say: Ukraine held new peace talks with American and European officials on Monday. Volodymyr Zelenskyy said they were not easy, and Russia says it hasn't agreed to widen the talks.
stories.stand: Zelenskyy says the next meeting will be in Berlin; the Kremlin says no date is set for the next round.
body: Ukraine held talks with US and European officials on Monday on ending the war, Al Jazeera reported. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the talks were not easy and that participants agreed to meet in Berlin.

Zelenskyy said representatives of France, Germany, Britain, Italy and Poland took full part. Russian presidential aide Yuri Ushakov said Russia had not agreed to expand the talks beyond the Russian, Ukrainian and US delegations.
US envoy Jared Kushner said progress was being made but important challenges remained. Ireland's foreign minister, Helen McEntee, said the EU had approved 113 new sanctions on Russia.

stories.head: Yemen's parliament votes to brand Houthis a terrorist group as fighting spreads
stories.say: Yemen's parliament has unanimously backed a bill designating the Houthis a terrorist organisation. The army says it carried out six hundred and sixty-one attacks on Houthi positions.
stories.stand: The army says it carried out 661 attacks on Houthi positions as the group pushes towards Aden.
body: Yemen's parliament unanimously approved a bill designating the Houthis a terrorist organisation, the state-run Saba news agency reported. It criminalises Houthi activities, financing and arms supply, and now goes to Presidential Leadership Council chairman Rashad al-Alimi.

Army spokesperson Colonel Majed al-Nuzaili said on Monday that government forces had carried out 661 attacks on Houthi positions in Taiz, Marib and al-Jawf, part of an offensive launched on 5 October.

The army says 173 Houthi fighters were killed or wounded. Those figures have not been independently verified. Government-aligned forces have pulled back from near the Bab al-Mandab strait to defend Aden.

stories.head: Quad leaders agree military drill and minerals deals in Manila
stories.say: Leaders of the US, Australia, India and Japan have agreed a joint military exercise and new critical minerals deals at their first Quad summit in two years, held in Manila.
stories.stand: It was the first leader-level Quad meeting since Donald Trump returned to the White House.
body: Donald Trump, Anthony Albanese, Narendra Modi and Sanae Takaichi met in Manila on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit, the first leader-level Quad talks in two years, ABC News reported.

Trump announced a joint military exercise involving maritime patrol aircraft and several critical minerals deals. The leaders also pledged more than US$85 million to widen access to AI among Indo-Pacific partners.
Albanese said China was not a factor behind the exercise. Trump travels on to Shenzhen, where talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are due on Thursday.

stories.head: Protests in the Philippines over Trump visit and US-backed AI hub
stories.say: Protesters in Manila have rallied against Donald Trump's visit and a US-backed plan for an AI and manufacturing hub north of the capital, which critics say will displace farmers.
stories.stand: Critics say the 4,000-acre Pax Silica site would displace farming communities and the Indigenous Aeta people.
body: Protests against Donald Trump's visit to the Philippines spread on Monday, CBS News reported. Many oppose a US-backed plan for an artificial intelligence and manufacturing hub of more than 4,000 acres just north of Manila.

The hub is linked to Pax Silica, a State Department-led initiative to secure non-Chinese supply chains for high-tech manufacturing. More than 25 countries have joined; the Philippines signed up in April.

The Marcos administration says the project could create 100,000 to 130,000 jobs. Critics say it would displace farming communities and the Indigenous Aeta people. Officials said no big announcements were expected during the visit.

stories.head: Mongolia's president says he will resign over railway bribery claims
stories.say: Mongolia's president, Khurelsukh Ukhnaa, says he will resign after claims he received twenty-five million dollars linked to a railway deal. He denies any wrongdoing.
stories.stand: Khurelsukh Ukhnaa denies wrongdoing; parliament is expected to vote on his resignation this week.
body: Mongolia's President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa said he will resign after accusations that he benefited financially from a government railway project, ITV News reported from AP.

A former Ulaanbaatar mayor, Nyambaatar Khishgee, alleged on Saturday that Khurelsukh received $25 million linked to the Tavantolgoi-Gashuunsukhait railway when he was prime minister. The company involved, Bodi International, denies paying bribes.
Khurelsukh denied wrongdoing and said he would cooperate with investigators. The resignation takes effect once parliament accepts it, with a vote expected this week.

stories.head: Australia sanctions Israeli settler leader Daniella Weiss
stories.say: Australia has sanctioned Daniella Weiss, a leading figure in Israel's settler movement, along with two other people and four organisations over settlement expansion in the West Bank.
stories.stand: Penny Wong said the measures target settlement expansion and abuses against Palestinians, a day after the UK hit settlement builders.
body: Australia has sanctioned three individuals and four entities over illegal settlement expansion and abuses against Palestinians in the West Bank, Foreign Minister Penny Wong announced on Wednesday.
They include Daniella Weiss and the Nachala movement she leads, as well as the Amana Settlement Association. The measures include travel bans and asset freezes.

On Tuesday the UK sanctioned eight construction and development firms building settlements, and the activist group Tzav 9. Israel's foreign minister Gideon Sa'ar called the UK move a hostile act and said Israel would respond.

stories.head: Man jailed for life over 2023 Dublin school knife attack
stories.say: Riad Bouchaker has been jailed for life for trying to murder three children outside a Dublin school in twenty twenty-three, an attack followed by the city's worst riots in decades.
stories.stand: Riad Bouchaker, 52, was convicted in July of attempting to murder three children outside a school in central Dublin.
body: Riad Bouchaker, 52, was sentenced to life imprisonment at the Central Criminal Court in Dublin on Monday for the attempted murder of three children, Al Jazeera reported.

He was found guilty in July of eight charges over the knife attack outside a school on 23 November 2023. Three children and a childcare worker were injured. The youngest girl, now eight, was left severely disabled.
The attack was followed by rioting and looting, the worst in the capital for decades, fuelled by false online claims about the attacker. Nearly 100 people were arrested.

stories.say: A Sudanese army air strike killed at least thirteen civilians, including women and children, in West Kordofan on Sunday, according to the rights group Emergency Lawyers.
stories.stand: Emergency Lawyers says homes were destroyed; Al Jazeera could not independently verify the report.
body: An air strike blamed on the Sudanese Armed Forces killed at least 13 civilians, including women and children, in West Kordofan state on Sunday, the rights group Emergency Lawyers said.
The group said several homes were destroyed and condemned the use of indiscriminate air strikes on residential areas. Al Jazeera said it could not immediately verify the report.
The war between the army and the Rapid Support Forces began in April 2023. At least 59,000 people have been killed and about 13 million displaced, according to reports cited by Al Jazeera.

stories.head: Costa Rican journalist who reported death threats is shot dead
stories.say: Costa Rican journalist Camilo Rodriguez, who accused politicians of links to drug traffickers, has been shot dead near San José. Prosecutors say it looked like a contract killing.
stories.stand: Police say two men on a motorcycle opened fire on Camilo Rodriguez on a highway outside San José.
body: Camilo Rodriguez, 50, an independent journalist who alleged links between drug traffickers and politicians, was shot dead on Monday in Santo Domingo de Heredia, outside San José, CBS News reported.
Police chief Raul Rivera said two men on a motorcycle opened fire. Attorney General Carlo Diaz said the scene resembled a contract killing and that Rodriguez had declined witness protection.
Rodriguez had reported several death threats from trafficking groups. President Laura Fernandez, who had sued him for defamation, called the killing a stain on freedom of expression.

stories.head: Paraguay's former president Santiago Peña moved to military jail
stories.say: Paraguay's former president Santiago Peña has been moved to a military prison after reports he enjoyed a private gym and dining room while awaiting trial in a bank corruption case.
stories.stand: A judge ordered the move after reports of special treatment while he awaits trial over the Ueno bank collapse.
body: Former Paraguayan President Santiago Peña was moved to Viñas Cué military prison on Monday on a judge's orders, Al Jazeera reported. Media had reported he had a large dining room, a private gym and other amenities in detention.

Peña was removed from office by impeachment on 6 November over the collapse of Ueno bank. Prosecutors accuse him of directing public funds to the bank while it made insider loans to its owners. He denies wrongdoing.
His successor, Pedro Alliana, said he had dismissed the officer accused of giving Peña special treatment.

stories.head: Border clashes in Ethiopia's Moyale disrupt trade and push thousands into Kenya
stories.say: Clashes between forces linked to Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regions have spread around Moyale, disrupting trade. The UN refugee agency says up to fifty thousand people crossed into Kenya.
stories.stand: The violence over a disputed regional border escalated in October and has spread to neighbouring districts.
body: Fighting between police and armed groups linked to Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regional administrations has disrupted daily life and the livestock trade in the southern Borana zone, Al Jazeera reported.
The violence escalated in Moyale in October after a Somali regional office was opened in a disputed area, and spread to Arero and Wachile.
The UN refugee agency said on 28 October that local authorities estimated up to 50,000 people had crossed into Kenya. A 2004 referendum left the Moyale boundary unresolved.

stories.say: Papua New Guinea has proposed a policy encouraging families to have no more than three children, as its population grows by more than a hundred and eighty thousand a year.
stories.stand: The proposal from James Marape's government is still at an early stage.
body: Papua New Guinea's government, led by Prime Minister James Marape, has proposed a national family planning policy encouraging families to have no more than three children, ABC News reported.
Official figures put the population at about 10.18 million, growing by more than 180,000 a year. Only 25% of women of reproductive age use modern contraception.
The policy is still a proposal. Its stated aims are to prevent unplanned pregnancies and ease pressure on government services and household budgets.

stories.head: First snow of the season hits northern England and Scotland
stories.say: More than an inch of snow fell in parts of the UK on Tuesday morning under the season's first snow warning, with two red flood warnings in Worcester and Stafford.
stories.stand: A Met Office snow warning ran from Staffordshire to south-west Scotland, and two red flood warnings were issued.
body: More than an inch of snow fell in parts of the UK on Tuesday morning, ITV News reported. The Met Office recorded 3cm at Spadeadam, near Carlisle.

The season's first snow warning covered an area from Staffordshire to south-west Scotland until 11am. Two red flood warnings were in place, for Barbourne Brook in Worcester and Sandyford Brook in Stafford.

A fallen tree blocked the line between Llandudno Junction and Holyhead. Sunday night was the coldest of the season so far, at -7.7C in Tulloch Bridge in the Highlands. A cold-health alert covers three northern English regions until 9am on Thursday.

stories.say: National Highways is ending its contract with speed camera supplier Verra Mobility, after a fault meant some drivers on England's motorways were wrongly caught speeding.
stories.stand: A review into the fault on variable speed cameras was published, and the Home Office has revoked the system's approval.
body: National Highways is ending its contract with speed camera supplier Verra Mobility after an anomaly in variable speed cameras on England's strategic road network, the Department for Transport said on Tuesday.

On rare occasions drivers had too little time to respond to a speed limit change, or were caught after it changed. Cameras on around 0.2% of roads in England were affected, and those identified have been offered redress.
The Home Office has revoked the system's type approval. An independent review by Tracy Westall was published on Tuesday, and its recommendations have been accepted.

stories.stand: Leigh Ross, 39, was remanded in custody after appearing before Leeds magistrates.
body: Leigh Ross, 39, of Harrogate, appeared at Leeds Magistrates' Court on Monday charged with two counts each of causing death by dangerous driving, driving while uninsured, driving while disqualified and taking a vehicle without consent, ITV News reported.
The charges follow a crash on Gelderd Road in Leeds at 12:44am on Sunday, in which a car being pursued by police hit another vehicle. Two people in that car, aged 22 and 23, died.
No plea was entered. Ross was remanded in custody to appear at Leeds Crown Court. The charges are allegations and have not been tested at trial.

stories.stand: Billy Stokoe's term rose from six years and nine months after the Attorney General called it unduly lenient.
body: The Court of Appeal has increased the sentence of Billy Stokoe, 20, from Sunderland, to eight years and six months, the Attorney General's Office said on Tuesday.

Stokoe hit an 86-year-old woman on a zebra crossing on Burdon Road in Sunderland in May 2025 while riding an illegal e-bike. He admitted causing death by dangerous driving and driving while unlicensed and uninsured, and was over the limit for cannabis.
He was originally given six years and nine months at Newcastle Crown Court. Attorney General Ellie Reeves referred the case under the Unduly Lenient Sentence scheme.

stories.say: Gavin Stephens, who leads the National Police Chiefs' Council, has backed government plans for fewer, larger police forces and a new national police service.
stories.stand: Gavin Stephens said the current 43-force system creates a postcode lottery in access to technology.
body: Gavin Stephens, chairman of the National Police Chiefs' Council, backed government plans for fewer, larger police forces and a new National Police Service in a speech in Westminster on Tuesday, ITV News reported.
He said police could not afford complacent nostalgia and that the current system creates a postcode lottery in access to technology and specialist support. England and Wales has 43 police forces.
Under the plans, counter-terrorism, some fraud and serious gang crime would move to the national service. Stephens said homicide fell 7% in the year to March 2026.

stories.head: Biometrics watchdog backs plans for facial recognition law
stories.say: The government plans to give facial recognition a statutory basis with a single new oversight body. The Biometrics Commissioner welcomed it but says key details are missing.
stories.stand: Professor William Webster says the consultation response is a clear direction of travel but lacks detail on oversight.
body: The Biometrics and Surveillance Camera Commissioner, Professor William Webster, has welcomed the government's response to its consultation on facial recognition, in a statement on Tuesday.

He said the response points towards primary legislation giving facial recognition a statutory legal basis, a single new oversight body with compliance powers, and new codes of practice for public services and the commercial sector.
Webster said live facial recognition is intrusive and needs clear safeguards. He said the response lacks detail on governance, national standards and whether the new body will be properly resourced.

body: Bogdan Gasparov, 40, a Moldovan national, was jailed for three years and six months at Chelmsford Crown Court on 9 November, ITV News Anglia reported.

He was found hiding in a loft at his home in Dagenham. He admitted theft and entering the UK in breach of a deportation order.

stories.stand: Wesley Rodrigues was arrested on Chelsea Bridge about 15 minutes after a Met Police drone was sent up.
body: Wesley Rodrigues, 18, of east London, was sentenced at Southwark Crown Court to 18 months in a young offender institution, ITV News reported. He admitted six thefts, dangerous driving, carrying an offensive weapon and having no insurance.

He had thrown a machete into the Thames before his arrest. He was also banned from driving for three years and 39 weeks.

stories.stand: The government endorsed the review and set up a Youth Opportunities Unit reporting to the prime minister.
body: Alan Milburn's review of young people and work, published on Tuesday, says a complete system reset is needed. The number of 16 to 24-year-olds not in education, employment or training topped one million earlier this year, ITV News reported.

body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday that the UK had lost more than it gained in the decade since Brexit, and that the hard Brexit deal was not good enough for Britain. He was speaking at the Lord Mayor's Banquet.

stories.stand: The changes, based on Denmark's system, would also disqualify 'bad faith' modern slavery claims used to delay removal.
body: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has tabled changes to the law to remove the notice period before failed asylum seekers are deported, ITV News reported. The system is based on one in Denmark.

Immigration officers would no longer have to give five working days' notice, and would have six months after a failed appeal to remove someone before further notice is needed. A new Independent Immigration Appeals Authority would be set up.
Border security minister Anna Turley said people who had exhausted their appeals should be removed promptly. People making bad faith modern slavery claims to delay removal would lose protections.

body: The UK will send more than 1,000 short-range air defence missiles and launchers, and more than a dozen air defence radars, to Ukraine this winter, the Ministry of Defence said on Tuesday.

Deliveries begin in mid-December. The missiles are made by Thales in Belfast. The UK, Sweden and Ukraine also signed a letter of intent on supplying Gripen fighter jets.

body: Robert White Jr., 44, a former DC City Council member, is the District of Columbia's new delegate to Congress, ITV News reported from AP. He succeeds Eleanor Holmes Norton, who is retiring after 36 years.

The speaker sets the legislative agenda and can convene parliament for a confidence vote. The opposition plans laws including an independent inquiry into the 7 October 2023 attacks and a two-term limit for prime ministers.

stories.stand: Vacancies fell to 690,000 and regular pay growth slowed to 3.5%, the Office for National Statistics said.
body: The UK unemployment rate fell to 4.6% in the three months to September, from 4.7%, the Office for National Statistics said on Tuesday. Most economists had expected no change, ITV News reported.
Job vacancies fell by 22,000 to 690,000, the biggest quarterly fall since June 2025. Payrolled employees fell by 34,000 in October to 30.2 million, a figure the ONS says may be revised.
Regular earnings growth eased to 3.5%. The ONS's Liz McKeown said the fall in vacancies was concentrated in smaller businesses, which cite higher costs.

Workers want the minimum monthly wage raised to 30,000 taka ($240) from 12,500 taka. About 500 of the country's 4,500 garment factories are shut, according to AFP sources.
The next wage board meeting is set for 23 November. Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter, and the industry employs more than four million people.

stories.stand: The International Meteor Organization expects the peak around 23:45 GMT on Tuesday.
body: The Leonid meteor shower peaks on the night of 17 to 18 November, with the International Meteor Organization expecting the peak around 23:45 GMT on Tuesday, Al Jazeera reported.
Under clear, dark skies, watchers may see up to about 15 meteors an hour. Leonids travel at about 71km a second, among the fastest meteors.
The Moon is about half full and sets around midnight in many places. The shower comes from the dust trail of Comet Tempel-Tuttle; the best viewing is between midnight and dawn.

stories.say: NASA's Terra satellite, designed to last six years, will stop collecting science data on the first of December after twenty-seven years, because of ageing systems and a drifting orbit.
stories.stand: The satellite, launched in December 1999, will be powered off in January 2027.
body: NASA's Terra mission will stop collecting science data on 1 December 2026, the agency said. All spacecraft systems will be shut down in January 2027.
Launched in December 1999 and designed to last six years, Terra has operated for 27 years. NASA cited ageing systems and a drifting orbit.
Its five instruments built long-term records of wildfires, land-use change, dust and smoke, atmospheric composition and ice cover. The data remain free to the public.

stories.say: Physicists at UC San Diego have used a new method on Planck satellite data and found the same tiny twist in the polarisation of the oldest light in the universe, about a third of a degree.
stories.stand: The result matches an earlier analysis, but researchers say it does not prove the light really rotated.
body: Researchers at the University of California San Diego have tested a hinted twist in the polarisation of the cosmic microwave background, the universe's oldest light, using a new method on Planck satellite data.
They estimated the so-called birefringence angle at 0.37 degrees, plus or minus 0.12, matching an established analysis. The study is in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.
The authors say the agreement does not confirm that the light actually rotated, since instrument misalignment could mimic the signal. If real, it could point to new physics such as axion-like fields.

stories.head: Neanderthal gene variant linked to lower schizophrenia risk
stories.say: A gene variant inherited from Neanderthals is linked to a slightly smaller visual cortex and, in people with two copies, a nearly ten per cent lower risk of schizophrenia, a study finds.
stories.stand: Nobel laureate Svante Pääbo co-led the study, published in PNAS.
body: A Neanderthal-derived gene variant near the DAAM1 gene is linked to altered brain structure and lower schizophrenia risk, according to a study in PNAS led by Hugo Zeberg and Svante Pääbo, Euronews reported.
Carriers have occipital lobes about 0.85 cubic centimetres smaller per copy. People with two copies have a nearly 10% lower risk of schizophrenia.
The variant appears unrelated to general intelligence. The authors say the findings caution against equating the size of a brain region with ability.

stories.say: Physicists in Munich and Innsbruck have found a way to put error margins on quantum simulators too large for ordinary computers to check, testing it on a chain of fifty-one ions.
stories.stand: The method was tested on 10 trapped ions, then scaled to a 51-ion chain.
body: Researchers from the Technical University of Munich and the University of Innsbruck have developed a way to give results from quantum simulators verifiable error margins, in a study published in Physical Review X.
The method uses experimental data to reconstruct how the simulator actually behaves, then carries the uncertainties into error limits on its results.

It was tested on 10 trapped ions, which classical computers can still check, then scaled to a 51-ion chain. Peter Zoller said quantum advantage should also be judged by how small a verifiable error a system can reach.

stories.stand: 2026 ED138 is the largest trans-Neptunian object found in about 20 years, researchers say.

It is estimated at 600 to 1,500km across and lies about 46 times as far from the Sun as Earth. Mario Jurić called it roughly 1,000km across, the largest such find in about 20 years.
It was found by Matthew Holman of the Harvard and Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics. More observations are needed to confirm whether it is round enough to be a dwarf planet.

stories.say: A University of Mississippi study of four hundred and fifty people found different psychopathic traits were linked to different word choices when people wrote about their highs and lows.
stories.stand: Researchers say the work is not meant to diagnose psychopathy from language.
body: Researchers at the University of Mississippi asked 450 people, including students and people who had been incarcerated, to write about their life's highs, lows and turning points, and then measured psychopathic traits.

People higher in disinhibition used more negative words and mentioned friends less. Those higher in meanness used more positive and achievement-related words, and boldness was linked to fewer anxiety words.
The study is in Personality and Individual Differences. The authors say it shows associations and is not a way to diagnose psychopathy.

stories.say: Physicists in Osaka have found electrons behaving as if they were much heavier than normal where a single atomic layer of ytterbium and copper meets a copper crystal.
stories.stand: Heavy fermion states are linked to unusual superconductivity, though none was shown here.
body: Researchers at the University of Osaka studied a single atomic layer of ytterbium and copper on a copper crystal and found a heavy fermion state, where electrons act as if they have far greater mass, according to a study in Communications Materials.
One such state extends from the layer into the copper below, which the team describes as the first direct evidence of heavy fermion behaviour produced across such an interface.
Heavy fermion states are linked to unconventional superconductivity, but the study did not demonstrate superconductivity. The team now aims to engineer and control these states.

stories.stand: The rocks at 'Idubi' are larger than earlier silica finds, allowing a detailed study.
body: NASA's Perseverance rover has found a cluster of bright rocks rich in hydrated silica at a site called Idubi, outside Jezero crater, the mission team wrote on NASA's science blog.
SuperCam data show the rocks are not igneous. On Earth, hydrated silica forms in watery settings such as hot springs and groundwater systems, and can preserve microfossils.
Earlier silica-rich rocks on Jezero's rim were too small to study closely. A detailed close-up campaign at Idubi is under way.

Different kinds of light are mapped to different sounds, such as X-rays to high tones. The project is led by the Chandra X-ray Center.

stories.stand: The University of Otago survey is the first full count of the endangered species.
body: A drone survey of erect-crested penguins, which breed only on the Bounty and Antipodes Islands south-east of New Zealand, counted about 27,800 breeding pairs on the Bounty Islands and 29,800 on the Antipodes, University of Otago researchers reported in PLOS ONE.
The Bounty population has been stable for at least 25 years, while the Antipodes population has fallen by more than 40% since 1995, even though the Antipodes are about 40 times larger.
The researchers suggest predation by skuas and stronger storms may be behind the decline. The species is listed as endangered.

stories.stand: The Pan American Health Organization says the US no longer meets the standard it first reached in 2000.
body: The Pan American Health Organization announced on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, which it first achieved in 2000, CBS News and ABC News reported.

The CDC has recorded 5,412 cases in 2026, more than double last year's 2,242, with more than 590 hospitalisations. The largest outbreak, in Pennsylvania, has passed 1,500 cases. CBS said 96% of this year's cases were unvaccinated or of unknown status.
Mexico and Bolivia also lost their status this year, and Canada in 2025. PAHO says vaccination coverage of at least 95% is the best way to keep measles out.

stories.stand: Shanghai authorities said his team failed to warn the hospital about safety problems seen in primate tests.
body: Neuroscientist Zilong Qiu has been dismissed as deputy director of a Shanghai Jiao Tong University-affiliated institute after a six-year-old girl died in his gene-editing trial, Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported, according to CBS News.

The girl, who had a rare neurodevelopmental condition, died in March 2025 from complications. Shanghai authorities found the team did not properly warn the hospital about safety issues from earlier primate tests.
Qiu's paper in Nature in February 2026 did not mention her death. He has been suspended from scientific projects for five years. AFP said he had not responded to requests for comment.

stories.say: A UN report warns that hormone-disrupting chemicals in plastics, cosmetics and pesticides are a growing threat to health, and most chemicals have never been checked.
stories.stand: The report says policies are fragmented and insufficient and calls for coordinated international action.
body: A report released on Tuesday by two UN bodies, including the UN Environment Programme, warns that endocrine-disrupting chemicals pose a growing threat to health, Euronews reported.

The chemicals are found in plastics, personal care products, toys, electronics and pesticides, and have been detected in breast milk and umbilical cord blood. Early exposure can affect brain development, growth and reproductive health.
Of more than 350,000 registered chemicals and mixtures, most have never been assessed for hormone-disrupting effects. The report calls for stronger regulation and safer alternatives.

stories.head: WHO says Europe is the only region to miss its target on women's smoking
stories.say: The World Health Organization says Europe is the only region that missed its goal of cutting women's tobacco use by thirty per cent, and that girls now smoke and vape as much as boys.
stories.stand: Women's tobacco use in the WHO European Region fell just 12% between 2010 and 2025.
body: The WHO European Region, covering 53 countries, is the only WHO region that missed the global target of a 30% cut in women's tobacco use by 2025, the World Health Organization said, according to Euronews.
Women's tobacco use fell from 19.6% to 17.3% between 2010 and 2025, a 12% drop, and is rising in 15 countries. Men's use fell 23%.
About 14% of 13 to 15-year-olds use e-cigarettes, roughly twice the global average. WHO Europe's Kristina Mauer-Stender said women and girls were being left far behind.

The authors suggest possible benefits for people with obesity or diabetes if treatment starts early, but say this is a hypothesis that needs testing.

The researchers say the results show associations only, that screen content probably matters more than duration, and that intervention studies are needed.

stories.stand: Use in poultry reached its lowest level on record, the Veterinary Medicines Directorate says.
body: Sales of antibiotics for animals in the UK rose 2% between 2024 and 2025 but remain 56% below 2014 levels, according to the Veterinary Medicines Directorate's annual report, published on Tuesday.

Antibiotic use in poultry meat production reached its lowest level to date, and use in pigs fell 11% on the year. Critically important antibiotics made up under 0.5% of sales for food-producing animals.

stories.stand: Australia, which leads the negotiations, says at least one more draft will come before talks end on Friday.
body: An 18-page draft cover decision published by Australia, which leads negotiations at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, includes a call for a fossil fuel phaseout, Arab News reported on Tuesday.

It also calls on wealthy nations to reach net zero by 2030. EU climate envoy Wopke Hoekstra said it had many characteristics of a shopping list and needed significant change. Australian minister Chris Bowen said it contained elements not all parties agree on.
The talks are due to end on Friday, and agreements need consensus. Turkey, which holds the presidency, wants a target to raise electricity's share of global energy demand to 35% by 2035.

The winners were Bhutan for protecting Himalayan forests, Mahindra Last Mile Mobility for electric rickshaws, Niue Ocean Wide Trust for marine protection, PFAS-Free France for campaigning against forever chemicals, and Ørsted for offshore wind.

stories.head: Manure-fuelled biogas now makes up about 40% of Denmark's gas grid
stories.say: Denmark now has about a hundred and fifty industrial biogas plants, largely fed by pig and cattle manure, giving it Europe's highest share of biogas in its gas grid, around forty per cent.
stories.stand: Campaigners say the model props up factory farming; the industry says it cuts unavoidable farm emissions.
body: Denmark has about 150 industrial-sized biogas plants, up from a handful a little over a decade ago, Al Jazeera reported. Up to 70% of their raw material comes from pig and cattle manure.
Biogas makes up about 40% of Denmark's gas grid, the highest share in Europe. In Sonderborg, two plants process about 850,000 tonnes of organic material a year.

stories.say: Portugal plans to help low-income families and very small businesses buy electric cars, with subsidies of up to fifteen thousand euros per household.
stories.stand: The plan still needs European Commission approval, and critics say it could pull people off public transport.
body: Portugal plans to support more than 20,000 electric vehicle purchases by vulnerable families and microenterprises, Euronews reported. Environment Minister Maria da Graça Carvalho announced the plan during the 2027 budget debate.
About €104.5 million is set aside for around 5,500 cars for vulnerable families, with subsidies of up to €15,000. Microenterprises get €228 million for about 13,700 vehicles.
A further €125.5 million would co-finance 700 electric buses. The scheme still needs European Commission approval.

stories.head: New material captures carbon from humid exhaust in lab tests
stories.say: Chemists at Oregon State University have made a material that captures carbon dioxide from humid exhaust gas, a common problem for carbon capture, though so far only in lab tests.
stories.stand: The Oregon State University material kept water and CO2 in separate parts of its pores.
body: Researchers at Oregon State University have developed a metal-organic framework, called BVR-X, that captures carbon dioxide from humid gas, according to a study in Angewandte Chemie.

Water vapour in industrial exhaust usually reduces the performance of such materials. In lab tests, BVR-X captured CO2 from a highly humid gas stream containing only 4% CO2, and kept working over dozens of cycles.
No pilot or industrial-scale testing has been reported. The work was partly funded by Saudi Aramco.

stories.say: Finland has published a roadmap at COP thirty-one for moving away from fossil fuels, aiming for carbon neutrality by twenty thirty-five, but without a legal deadline to phase them out.
stories.stand: Over 96% of Finland's electricity already comes from non-fossil sources.
body: Finland has published a national roadmap for transitioning away from fossil fuels at the COP31 summit in Antalya, Euronews reported. It aims to be carbon neutral by 2035.

The plan does not set a legally binding deadline for phasing out fossil fuels. More than 96% of Finland's electricity already comes from non-fossil sources, and fossil fuels made up 18% of its energy mix in 2025.
It follows similar roadmaps from France, Germany and the Netherlands. Oil Change International said roadmaps need to be more than a restatement of existing policies.

stories.head: Study finds health risks in East Java villages that burned imported plastic
stories.say: Researchers in East Java say at least one in five of more than four thousand people studied in villages that burned plastic waste are at high risk of heart and lung disease.
stories.stand: Much of the plastic came mixed with imported paper and cardboard waste, including from Australia.
body: In villages in East Java, Indonesia, plastic separated from imported paper and cardboard waste was sold as fuel or burned in limestone kilns, ABC News reported.

A study of more than 4,000 people in six villages found at least 20% at high risk of cardiovascular disease and chronic lung disease. A researcher said many residents did not know burning plastic was dangerous.
Australia exported 701,000 tonnes of paper and cardboard to Indonesia in the latest financial year. Indonesia's environment ministry says it aims for comprehensive waste management by 2029.

stories.head: Less Arctic sea ice linked to summer droughts in eastern Europe
stories.say: A Romanian-led study links lower winter sea ice in the Barents and Kara seas to more summer drought across a band from Romania and Ukraine to Kazakhstan.
stories.stand: The University of Bucharest study used weather data going back to 1940.
body: Less winter sea ice in the Barents and Kara seas is linked to more summer drought across a wide area of Eurasia, a study led by Petru Vaideanu of the University of Bucharest found, Euronews reported. It is published in Frontiers in Water.
The affected zone stretches from eastern Romania, Moldova and Ukraine to western Kazakhstan. The team used ERA5 weather data from 1940 and adjusted for rising carbon dioxide.
The researchers suggest less sea ice is followed by a wavier atmospheric circulation that can bring warm, dry air and fewer clouds.

stories.head: US moves to stop Chinese firms renting AI chips in third countries
stories.say: The US Commerce Department will require export licences for advanced chips shipped to five countries including Singapore and Malaysia, to stop Chinese firms renting AI computing power there.
stories.stand: Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil are now treated as an unacceptable risk of diversion.
body: The US Bureau of Industry and Security announced on Monday new rules to stop Chinese AI developers evading export controls by remotely using data centres in third countries, Al Jazeera reported.

Anyone shipping advanced chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand or Brazil now needs an export licence. Until now, Chinese firms could legally rent top computing power remotely in some of those countries.

The Commerce and Justice departments confirmed a criminal investigation into Singapore data centre firm Megaspeed. Singapore said it does not condone using the country to get around other nations' laws.

stories.stand: Any decision at the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons review needs consensus, so one country can block it.
body: The seventh review conference of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons began discussions in Geneva on Monday on whether to launch negotiations on a binding agreement on lethal autonomous weapons, Euronews reported.

Decisions need consensus, so any single country can block a deal. Campaign group Stop Killer Robots says 130 countries support new rules. Seven countries, including Austria, Brazil and Ireland, proposed starting negotiations.
Russia's foreign ministry called restrictions premature. The US and Russia reportedly want to limit any restrictions.

stories.stand: Anders Engman covered the uprising aged 23 for a Swedish weekly.
body: An open-air exhibition of photographs of the 1956 Hungarian revolution by Swedish photojournalist Anders Engman opened in the garden of Hungary's National Museum in Budapest on Monday, Euronews reported.

His widow, Inga-Britt Liljeroth, holds several hundred more photos from the revolution. A museum deputy director called the images key documents of the revolution.

stories.stand: Weather forced the team to skip the middle of the route on South Georgia.
body: TV historian Dan Snow was treated for early-stage hypothermia during a storm on a glacier in South Georgia, ITV News reported. His clothing froze in a sudden blizzard, and he improved after about 12 hours in a special sleeping bag.
Snow was retracing part of Sir Ernest Shackleton's 1916 crossing of the island for a History Hit documentary, with a team of eight including explorer Preet Chandi.
Bad weather forced them back from the middle section. They completed the first and final quarters and reached Stromness. Snow called the experience frightening.

stories.say: Two-time Formula One champion Fernando Alonso will race the Dakar Rally in January for Aston Martin, seven years after his first attempt, alongside Sebastien Loeb.
stories.stand: The 45-year-old will drive the Aston Martin Dreadnought, with five-time Dakar winner Marc Coma as co-driver.
body: Fernando Alonso, 45, will compete in the 2027 Dakar Rally for Aston Martin, Al Jazeera reported. He will drive the Aston Martin Dreadnought, run with Prodrive, with Marc Coma as co-driver.
The three-car team also includes Sebastien Loeb and Lucas Moraes. The rally runs from 9 to 23 January, mainly in Morocco, after moving from Saudi Arabia over security concerns.
Alonso finished 13th on his only previous Dakar, in 2020. He said Formula One remains his priority.

stories.head: Diallo says he has support beyond Europe in bid to unseat Infantino
stories.say: France's football federation president Philippe Diallo, Europe's candidate to unseat Gianni Infantino, says he has strong support beyond Europe. He'd need a hundred and six votes to win.
stories.stand: Candidates must declare by Wednesday; the election is at the FIFA Congress in Rabat in March.
body: Philippe Diallo, president of the French Football Federation and UEFA's candidate to challenge Gianni Infantino, said in Paris on Tuesday he had received signs of strong support from outside Europe, Al Jazeera reported.
He said 106 votes are needed to win. FIFA has 211 member associations, each with one vote; UEFA has 55.
Candidates must declare by Wednesday. The election is at the FIFA Congress in Rabat on 18 March 2027. The Asian Football Confederation has endorsed Infantino.

stories.head: Socceroos beaten 2-0 by Jordan as Popovic's future hangs in balance
stories.say: Australia lost two-nil to Jordan in a friendly in Doha, with Daniel Arzani sent off. Coach Tony Popovic called the first half terrible, ahead of talks on his future.
stories.stand: Tony Popovic, whose contract runs out, called it a reality check.
body: Jordan beat Australia 2-0 in a friendly in Doha, ABC News reported. Mousa Al-Taamari scored in the first half and Ali Olwan added a second in stoppage time.
Patrick Beach saved an Al-Taamari penalty, and Daniel Arzani was sent off for two yellow cards. Australia had beaten Qatar 3-0 two days earlier.
Coach Tony Popovic, who had said this could be his last game in charge, called the first half terrible. He is due to hold contract talks with Football Australia.

stories.head: Portugal coach Jorge Jesus hits back at Ronaldo's mother
stories.say: Portugal coach Jorge Jesus has responded to criticism from Cristiano Ronaldo's mother, asking if he now has to answer her, before Portugal's Nations League game in Wales.
stories.stand: Portugal need a point in Cardiff to top their Nations League group after losing 4-1 to Denmark.
body: Portugal coach Jorge Jesus asked on Tuesday whether he now had to respond to Cristiano Ronaldo's mother, after Dolores Aveiro said she was glad he had suffered his first defeat, Al Jazeera reported.
Portugal lost 4-1 to Denmark on Saturday, their first defeat since Ronaldo quit international football after a falling-out with Jesus.
Ronaldo holds world records of 234 caps and 146 goals in men's international football. Portugal need a point against Wales in Cardiff to top Nations League Group A4.

stories.head: South Africa slip after Bavuma injury as rain halts Johannesburg Test
stories.say: South Africa lost three quick wickets after captain Temba Bavuma retired hurt, closing fourteen runs behind Bangladesh before rain ended play in Johannesburg.
stories.stand: Litton Das took six catches, a Bangladesh Test record, after scoring a century.
body: South Africa reached 386 for seven at stumps on day three of the first Test against Bangladesh at the Wanderers in Johannesburg, 14 runs behind Bangladesh's 400, Gulf Times reported. Rain and lightning ended play after lunch on Tuesday.
Captain Temba Bavuma retired hurt on 49 with a calf injury. South Africa then slid from 358 for four to 373 for seven. Hasan Mahmud took four for 72.
Wicketkeeper Litton Das, who scored a century, took six catches, a Bangladesh Test record. Ryan Rickelton is unbeaten on 56.

stories.head: Scotland edge Wallabies 15-12 at Murrayfield
stories.say: Scotland beat Australia fifteen-twelve at Murrayfield in the Nations Championship, a fourth straight defeat for the Wallabies. Finn Russell kicked the decisive penalty.
stories.stand: Finn Russell's late penalty settled a tight Nations Championship Test.
body: Scotland beat Australia 15-12 at Murrayfield in the Nations Championship on Sunday, ABC News reported. It was the Wallabies' fourth straight defeat.
Matt Fagerson and Jack Dempsey scored tries for Scotland, and Finn Russell kicked a penalty in the 74th minute. Harry Potter and Max Jorgensen scored Australia's tries.
Rory Darge was named player of the match. Australia play Wales in Cardiff next.

stories.head: Britain to face Germany in Davis Cup Finals quarter-final in Bologna
stories.say: Great Britain will play Germany in the Davis Cup Finals quarter-finals in Bologna next week, with Cam Norrie in Leon Smith's team. The final is on the twenty-ninth of November.
stories.stand: Leon Smith's team includes Cam Norrie and Arthur Fery; the event runs from 24 to 29 November.
body: Great Britain will face Germany in the quarter-finals of the Davis Cup Finals in Bologna, the Lawn Tennis Association said. The eight-team knockout runs from 24 to 29 November.
Captain Leon Smith has picked Arthur Fery, Cam Norrie, Henry Patten and Neal Skupski. The other quarter-finals are Czechia against Canada, Italy against South Korea, and Austria against Spain.
The final is on Sunday 29 November.
